👵 The state pension age is climbing to 67. For a 66-year-old bricklayer whose body has already clocked off, that means a year on standard Universal Credit — about £425 a month.

The cross-party Work and Pensions Committee says the wait will 'harm' those who cannot keep working, and the fix costs £600 million — against £10.5 billion the Treasury banks from the rise. People who worked fifty years deserve better than a means-tested waiting room.
